panels.text: According to Charles Duhigg, every habit has a loop: a cue, a routine and a reward.
For example, a TV programme ends (cue), you go to the fridge (routine), you eat a snack (reward).
A cue can be a prior action, a time of day, a location, or anything you associate with the habit.
The key to changing a habit is to identify the cue and modify the routine and reward. Old habits may come back when old cues return, which is called habit renewal.

probes.question: In the habit loop, what triggers the routine?
True or false: a habit that seems to have gone can re-emerge when its old cues are reintroduced.
